cards.headline: Haze in Singapore: Runners train in malls, families head for indoor playgrounds
bullets: Singapore has had bad air quality for 13 days straight, the longest since 2015.
Runners are now training inside malls and doing indoor exercises like yoga.
Families are taking their kids to indoor playgrounds to escape the haze.
Several running events, including the Great Eastern Women's Run, have been cancelled due to poor air quality.

cards.headline: Hom Yoga to close permanently following Valley Point redevelopment, Orchard Central exit
bullets: Hom Yoga will close its last studio at Valley Point on March 21, 2027.
The River Valley mall is being redeveloped, leading to the studio's closure.
Hom Yoga had already closed its Orchard Central branch in November.
Rising costs and difficulty finding a new space contributed to the decision.
Customers can use existing packages until the final closing date.

cards.headline: ‘Failure points you to the solution’: Students win HTX award for pushing past setbacks in research
bullets: Students won an award for pushing through research problems and not giving up.
One student developed an AI to predict cancer treatment success using patient data.
Another student used chicken bones to clean dye pollution from water.
The award recognizes students who learn from setbacks in science projects.
Winners get $4,000 and a chance to intern with HTX.

cards.headline: Home buyers using more cash and CPF for down payment even as mortgage loans rise
bullets: Nearly 8 in 10 buyers of new private homes took loans of $1 million or more.
Home prices rose 49% for new private homes, but loans only grew 35%.
Buyers are using more cash or CPF for down payments instead of borrowing more.
Fewer buyers are borrowing the maximum loan amount allowed for their property purchase.

cards.headline: F&B businesses struggle as haze conditions worsen
bullets: Tekka Centre had half empty seats on October 16 due to bad air.
Some food stall owners are considering closing their businesses because of the haze.
Footfall at Tekka Centre dropped by about 30% since the haze started.
Hawkers say business can fall by a third on bad haze days.
Some customers are avoiding outdoor eateries due to the poor air quality.

cards.headline: Singapore haze: Air quality remains very unhealthy in west, unhealthy in other regions
bullets: Air quality in western Singapore hit a very unhealthy 230 PSI on Sunday, the highest this year.
Haze levels improved slightly in the afternoon but remained unhealthy in other parts of the island.
Smoke haze from fires in Indonesia is expected to continue drifting towards Singapore.
Several outdoor events were cancelled or postponed due to the poor air quality.
Health advisories suggest using 1-hour PM2.5 readings to decide on wearing masks.

cards.headline: BigBang XX: Cosmos in Singapore – a triumphant return for the K-pop legends
bullets: K-pop legends BigBang returned to Singapore for their first concert in 10 years.
Thousands of fans filled the National Stadium for the XX: Cosmos show.
The trio performed many of their hit songs and solo tracks.
Members G-Dragon, Daesung, and Taeyang showcased their individual talents.
The energetic crowd sang along throughout the three-hour performance.

cards.headline: Rival ports 'fast catching up': SM Lee warns against complacency, says port workers must not face shift alone
bullets: Rival ports are catching up, and some might even be ahead of Singapore's port.
SM Lee warned against becoming complacent and losing business to competitors.
He stressed the need for technological upgrades and worker training.
Strong cooperation between management, unions, and workers is crucial for success.
Past challenges required difficult choices, painful adjustments, and retraining of workers.

cards.headline: These marathon runners will give up their personal best to save a life
bullets: 238 trained runners will act as first responders at the Singapore International Marathon.
These 'medic runners' will help participants needing medical aid, like CPR.
They must put helping others above their own race time.
The new category was inspired by similar races overseas.
Medic runners were selected from over 1,300 applicants.

cards.headline: From weekend markets to a matcha network: How Kevin Chee built Matchaya
bullets: Matchaya founder Kevin Chee built his business by selling bottled matcha lattes at weekend markets.
He quit his bank job to open the first Matchaya outlet in 2014.
Matchaya now supplies about half the matcha used by cafes and restaurants in Singapore.
The business also distributes matcha from Japan and China to commercial clients.
Matchaya's new flagship store offers a more hands-on experience and Japanese-inspired food.

cards.headline: Australian home auctions decline as rate hikes dampen activity
bullets: Just 1,423 homes were auctioned in Australian capital cities last week, down 18.6% from the week before.
This is about 46% fewer homes auctioned than at the same time last year.
The rate of homes selling at auction this spring is lower than the average for winter.
Higher interest rates are making fewer people want to buy homes in Australia.

cards.headline: 2026 BMW i7 review: Buyers of BMW’s flagship have one surprising trait
bullets: The new electric BMW i7 50 can travel up to 728km on a full charge.
The petrol version, 735, starts at S$684,888 including COE.
The car has a new display strip along the windscreen for information.
Most buyers of this luxury car still prefer to drive themselves.
It offers a smooth ride but can handle fast corners well.

cards.headline: Ferrari’s S$2.1 million EV trips the light fantastic
bullets: Ferrari's first electric car, the S$2.1 million Luce, is now in Singapore.
It's a five-seater with four doors and a large boot, unlike previous Ferraris.
The car accelerates to 100 kmh in 2.5 seconds and has a range of over 530 km.
Ferrari focused on making the electric car fun to drive and sound exciting.

cards.headline: Good Class Bungalow market activity picks up pace on ‘realistic’ pricing
bullets: Good Class Bungalow sales are picking up as prices become more realistic.
Buyers are looking for good deals on luxury homes.
The market was slower earlier in the year due to global uncertainty.
Buyers are more selective and want better value for their money.

cards.headline: Celine Dion, Harry Styles concerts get an AI sound upgrade
bullets: A French company uses AI to make concert sound clearer by filtering out noise.
This new tech helps singers' voices stand out from instruments and crowd noise.
It has been used for big names like Celine Dion and Harry Styles.
The system can reduce unwanted sound by up to 40 decibels.
The company expects a big jump in sales next year.

cards.headline: Elderly Holland Village cobbler shows up for work despite haze, S'pore woman calls for support
bullets: An elderly cobbler continues working in Holland Village despite the haze.
He has been repairing shoes for decades and needs customers.
A woman shared a video asking people to support his business.
He can be found near Wu Chun Po Bakery daily from 11am to 8pm.

cards.headline: Filipino helper, 35, worked in law firm for 8 years before coming to S'pore, hopes to one day study law
bullets: A Filipino domestic helper worked in a law firm for eight years in the Philippines.
She came to Singapore two years ago after her initial plans to work in Europe did not work out.
She is currently pursuing two engineering diplomas and hopes to one day study law.
She works on her studies during her days off and rest time.

cards.headline: Woman, 77, dies in PIE hit-and-run; minibus driver, 66, arrested
bullets: A 77-year-old woman died after being hit by a minibus on the PIE.
The minibus driver, 66, left the scene before police arrived.
Police later arrested the driver for causing death by careless driving.

cards.headline: This Warehouse Sale At Khatib Has Viral Squishies From $2 & Pay-By-Weight Crockery For $0.88/100g
bullets: Squishies start from $2 each at a warehouse sale in Khatib.
You can buy crockery by weight for $0.88 per 100g.
Home essentials are on sale from $1.
The sale runs until October 18th at HomeTeamNS Khatib.

cards.headline: A New Cinnamoroll-Themed Attraction Is Coming To Tokyo This November For A Limited Time Only
bullets: A Cinnamoroll-themed pop-up park opens in Tokyo from November 20, 2026, to January 17, 2027.
The attraction features a 12m long Cinnamoroll slide and interactive games.
Visitors can enjoy themed zones for Cinnamoroll's friends like Cappuccino and Chiffon.
Special experiences include a virtual tea party and exclusive merchandise sales.
Tickets cost around S$13 to S$20, with a separate charge for the virtual tea party.
